comments.body:
## Implemented — commit `60fb04aa0b7`, pending Gerrit

**Both copy sites now share three helpers in `_dc_fixtures.py`**, so the duplicated copy in `test_multi_project_rehearsal.py` cannot drift from the one behind `dc_store_copy_repo`:

- `store_copy_entries(listing, limit=200)` — all store metadata, all bridge-named directories, and canonical-id tickets sampled at an **even stride**. A head or tail slice would silently narrow the rehearsal to the oldest or newest tickets; the stride spans the store's whole history.
- `extract_store_snapshot(...)` — streams `git archive` into `tar -x` through a pipe, so the snapshot is never held whole in RAM on top of the copy on disk.
- `reclaim(work)` — both fixtures became `yield` fixtures and delete their tree at teardown, so concurrent modules stop summing their peaks.

**The guarantee is checked on every commit, not on the live lane.** `tests/unit/test_dc_store_copy_bounded_25e0.py` builds two real temporary tickets branches — one at the limit, one 20x larger — runs the fixture's own extraction against both, and asserts the copies are byte-identical in size. Before the fix that comparison would have shown the large store costing ~20x. No Jira, no CI provider, no live spend.

**Two real bugs the oracle caught while being written**, both fixed:

1. `Popen.__exit__` closes the pipes, so reading `archive.stderr` after the `with` raised `ValueError: read of closed file` — git's message, the entire point of reporting a failed archive, was unreachable. Now read inside the context.
2. `store_copy_entries` originally imported `is_ticket_entry` from `_dc_support`. That module calls `live_jira_ready()` **at import time**, which the repo tier forbids, so the helper was untestable off the live lane. The predicate is now local, and `test_the_local_ticket_entry_rule_matches_the_harnesss_own` compares the two functions' return expressions **by AST** so they cannot drift without failing.

**Coverage is not weakened.** The copy is still a real scrubbed store extracted from the live `tickets` branch — `test_the_bounded_slice_still_carries_real_tickets_and_store_metadata` asserts genuine extracted event files, not just entry names. `test_the_store_copy_is_complete_and_scrubbed` still catches a partial extraction; it now compares against the slice the fixture selected, and its docstring says so.

**Open until the live lane runs.** AC5 (no `running out of disk space` in a green run's log) can only be closed by a green `Live External Integration` run, which is scheduled rather than on-demand. Everything else is verified locally.

compiled_state.description:
## Symptom

The `Live External Integration` workflow's `jira DC harness smoke` job fails on
[run 35508005436](https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/35508005436) because the
GitHub-hosted runner runs out of disk, not because anything about Jira or the bridge is
wrong.

The runner warns first, then git fails, then the runner's own logging fails:

```
##[warning]You are running out of disk space. The runner will stop working when the
machine runs out of disk space. Free space left: 23 MB

fatal: sha1 file '/home/runner/work/_temp/rebar-basetemp/test_promote_only_binding_is_o0/
dc-multi-store-copy/.tickets-tracker/.git/index.lock' write error. Out of diskspace

subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command '['git', 'commit', '-q', '--no-verify', '-m',
'scrubbed store copy for 368f DC rehearsal']' returned non-zero exit status 128

##[error]No space left on device :
'/home/runner/actions-runner/cached/2.337.0/_diag/pages/491cc8e3-...log'
```

So the `git commit` exit 128 is ENOSPC with its own stderr naming it, rather than a
git-semantics failure — the diagnosis does not rest on inference.

The job otherwise reached a healthy state before dying: Jira DC came up and four projects
(`RBJFTJP`, `RBJYIPQ`, `RBJUAGO`, `RBJQDHV`) provisioned their Epic fields in ~0.03s each.
The harness is fine. It is the disk that is not.

## Root cause

The DC rehearsal fixtures copy the **entire live tickets branch** into the runner's temp
directory, once per test, and each copy costs roughly twice the store's working-tree size.

`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_multi_project_rehearsal.py:210-237`:

```python
work = tmp_path / "dc-multi-store-copy"
...
archive = run_git(["git", "archive", "FETCH_HEAD"], cwd=source).stdout
subprocess.run(["tar", "-x", "-C", str(tracker)], input=archive, check=True)
scrub_bridge_state(tracker)
_init(tracker, "tickets")
subprocess.run(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=tracker, check=True)
subprocess.run(["git", "commit", ...], cwd=tracker, check=True)
```

Three costs stack, all proportional to store size and none bounded:

1. `git archive FETCH_HEAD` materializes the **whole branch as a byte string in RAM**
   (`.stdout`) before anything is written.
2. `tar -x` writes a full working-tree copy to disk.
3. `git add -A` + `git commit` then writes a **second** full copy into the new repo's
   object database, so each fixture instance costs ~2x the tree on disk.

The store measured **1.5 GB** of working tree on 2026-09-20. A hosted `ubuntu-24.04`
runner has roughly 14 GB free after the image, and this job additionally hosts a
Dockerized Jira Data Center plus its database. Three separate modules perform this copy —
`test_multi_project_rehearsal.py`, `test_dc_mutations.py`, and
`test_store_copy_isolation.py` — each into its own `tmp_path`, and pytest retains recent
`tmp_path` trees rather than deleting them immediately.

This is why the failure is new rather than a flake: the cost is a function of store size,
and the store grows monotonically with every ticket event. The job has been getting closer
to the limit on every run and has now crossed it. It will not recover on its own, and a
rerun is not a remedy.

## Approach

Stop copying the whole store to exercise a store copy. The fixtures need a scrubbed,
writable store that is representative — not a byte-complete replica of every ticket ever
written. Two independent reductions, either of which alone restores headroom, and which
compose:

- Bound what is copied, so cost stops tracking total store size.
- Avoid paying for the copy twice by not re-committing a full working tree into a fresh
  object database when a cheap history-free copy would do.

Reclaiming each fixture's tree once the test finishes keeps concurrent modules from
summing their peaks.

The fix must not weaken what these tests prove: they exist to round-trip a **real**
scrubbed store through live Jira DC, so substituting synthetic tickets would relocate the
coverage gap rather than close it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Peak disk used by a DC rehearsal fixture does not scale with total store size. Verified by running the fixture against two stores of very different sizes and comparing peak usage.
- [ ] The store snapshot is not buffered whole in memory. Verified by reading the changed code for the `git archive` stdout capture.
- [ ] Each fixture's copy is reclaimed when its test finishes, so concurrent modules do not sum their peaks. Verified by asserting the path is gone after teardown.
- [ ] The tests still round-trip a REAL scrubbed store against live Jira DC, not synthetic tickets. Verified by reading the fixture for the live-branch source.
- [ ] The job completes without a runner disk warning. Verified by the absence of `running out of disk space` in a green run's log.
- [ ] The fix requires no single CI provider. Verified by reading the changed code for GitHub Actions specifics; the fixtures must behave the same locally.

## Verification

A green `Live External Integration` run whose log contains no
`You are running out of disk space` warning, plus a recorded `df` delta for the rehearsal
step showing peak usage independent of store size.
compiled_state.title: Jira DC harness exhausts the runner disk by copying the whole 1.5 GB ticket store per test
